title: Policy approval core
description: Objective: implement four-outcome policy evaluation, R0-R3 risk tiers, exact-hash approval decisions, and selective invalidation. Deliverable: packages/core policy modules with decision-table and property tests. NOT in scope: mutable UI policy editing, budgets, provider execution, or global speed modes. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Planning graph lifecycle core. Owned paths: packages/core/src/policy/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: Policy produces ALLOW, REQUIRE_APPROVAL, DENY, or HOLD_UNKNOWN with stable reason codes.
Unknown or missing inputs can never become ALLOW and caller risk labels cannot lower daemon-derived risk.
Approvals bind exact hashes/scope/policy/actor and invalidate only the proven impact set.
The focused core typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/policy/policy-decision-table.test.ts (<=250). Decision-table matrix (DoD 1/2): every outcome reachable with stable local reason codes; UNKNOWN/missing required inputs NEVER yield ALLOW under ANY permutation; riskHint matrix — SETTLEMENT effectiveTier = max(computedTier, callerRiskHint) ('cannot lower' constrains the floor; raising is pure tightening under the 699 fail-closed doctrine; computedTier/callerRiskHint/effectiveTier all recorded separately) INCLUDING the mandatory case hint=R2 + missing required fact -> STILL HOLD_UNKNOWN (a hint never rescues missing facts and never enters computedTier or the fact digest); dominance lattice DENY > HOLD_UNKNOWN > REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL > ALLOW; child-tighten composition — modeled as an ordered policy-SLICE chain fold (root->node; design 255/580/460: node-slice composition along the graph, not an abstract tree) with a relaxation-detected reason code when a child slice removes/weakens a parent rule or obligation absent a matching waiver; WAIVER shape enforced: {waiverRef, namedObligationId resolving to kind=SOFT, scope subset-of decision scope, expiry covering evaluation time, humanApprovalRef} — and a waiver NEVER converts HOLD_UNKNOWN to ALLOW (design 712 'cannot turn UNKNOWN into verified'); R2/R3 human-only (auto path structurally unavailable); R3 reason-required + step-up ref; EVERY human ApprovalDecision carries stepUpAuthRef (design 718 scopes step-up to all human approvals, not R3-only — record-level ref; verification is session/daemon-side, documented); no blanket-ALLOW path exists. Confirm RED.
implementationPlan.note:
RED CONFIRMED. `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exit 1: "Error: Cannot find module './policy-evaluation.js'" — 1 failed | 9 passed (10 files), 189 pre-existing tests still passing (no foreign breakage). File is 249 lines (<=250).

12 decision-table cases written against the not-yet-existing surface (evaluatePolicy + policy-contract types):
1. Every outcome reachable with a stable local reason code — ALLOW/ALLOWED_BY_POLICY, DENY/DENIED_BY_RULE, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL/HUMAN_ONLY_TIER, HOLD_UNKNOWN/REQUIRED_FACT_MISSING.
2. UNKNOWN-never-ALLOW over 8 permutations: absent required fact; truthClass UNKNOWN; OBSERVED; AGENT_REPORTED; tier-less fact; hint+absent; waiver+absent; waiver+UNKNOWN. The last two are the waiver-laundering paths (design 712) folded into the same permutation table rather than a separate case.
3/4/5. riskHint settlement: hint R3 raises effectiveTier while computedTier stays R0; hint R0 CANNOT lower a computed R2; hint appears in neither inputFacts nor usedFactIds; and the mandatory case hint=R2 + missing fact -> still HOLD_UNKNOWN with computedTier/effectiveTier both null.
6. Lattice DENY > HOLD_UNKNOWN > REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL > ALLOW asserted pairwise.
7. Slice-chain relaxation refused across four shapes: effect weakened DENY->ALLOW; parent obligation dropped; obligation kind downgraded HARD->SOFT; child ADDING an auto-approval opt-in the parent lacks (adding an opt-in is a relaxation, so the effective opt-in set can only shrink down the chain).
8. Waiver accepted ONLY when {namedObligationId resolves to a parent SOFT obligation, scope subset-of decision scope, expiry strictly after evaluatedAtEpochMs, humanApprovalRef non-empty}; four invalid shapes each -> DENY, and out-of-scope additionally carries WAIVER_INVALID.
9. Auto path structurally unavailable above R1: a forged R2 opt-in is an INPUT_INVALID REJECTION (not a decision), and R2/R3 facts yield REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL even with an R1 opt-in present.
10. R3 carries HARD obligations core.decision_reason_required + core.step_up_authentication_required; a slice with no opt-in defaults to REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL/AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (no blanket-ALLOW path).
11. Provenance recorded (policyRevisionRef, evaluatorVersion, action, graphNodeRevisionRefs, decisionDigest, matchedRuleIds), record + nested arrays deep-frozen, repeat evaluation deep-equal.
12. Malformed input -> INPUT_INVALID (null input, non-hex64 digest, NaN clock, duplicate factId, empty slice chain). INPUT_INVALID is sourceless in the registry, so this is the code that actually surfaces rather than degrading.

Two design settlements the test now pins, both fail-closed and documented in step-3's module header:
- A tier-contributing fact must clear the strongTruth floor (DAEMON_VERIFIED|HUMAN_APPROVED). OBSERVED/AGENT_REPORTED are not daemon-derived, so they are "unclassifiable" per design 11.6 and yield HOLD_UNKNOWN rather than grounding a tier.
- No tier-contributing fact at all -> computedTier null -> HOLD_UNKNOWN. Absence of classification is never silently R0.

Decision-table tests fully green.

TDD red then green — src/policy/approval-invalidation.test.ts + src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts (each <=250). Approval lifecycle: PENDING -> DECIDED|WITHDRAWN (WITHDRAWN terminal, no outgoing edges); decision APPROVE|REJECT immutable once DECIDED; validity projection CURRENT -> INVALIDATED | SUPERSEDED, never backward. SELECTIVE INVALIDATION (DoD 3): takes a SUPPLIED deterministic impact set (the graph diff computation is the scheduler/daemon's job per design 265 — validate-and-apply only): invalidates ONLY approvals whose bound hashes/scope intersect the impact set — non-intersecting approvals BIT-IDENTICAL after (property-asserted); impact-set input inherits the unknown-canonicalization refusal (design 250/265: hashes carry canonicalizer versions; unknown version -> refuse, fail closed). SUPERSEDED path: applied ONLY via an explicit successor-approval linkage input (a new revision's approval marks its predecessor SUPERSEDED — design 263/269 'old approval bytes are never relabeled'), DISTINCT from impact-set intersection -> INVALIDATED. Carry-forward invalidation conditions per design 265, all six: any mismatch, missing dependency, changed applicable policy slice, changed predecessor result, changed environment/runtime closure, unknown canonicalization -> carry-forward INVALID. Lifecycle rejections: ILLEGAL_TRANSITION from {aggregate:'APPROVAL'} with exact-code assertions (this test file is where the silent-degrade assertions live). Both files green.
